subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar own an opt-in persistent feature that executes user-configured local binaries when quota and provider events occur?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally constrained, but accepting a new local code-execution and event-metadata disclosure boundary is a repository-level product and security choice that patch correctness alone cannot settle.

options.title: Sponsor after argv repair
options.body: Accept the opt-in direct-exec design after the settings editor preserves argument boundaries and focused proof covers the repaired round trip.

options.title: Narrow the surface
options.body: Allow hooks only through manually edited configuration and CLI tooling, omitting the settings editor until a safer structured UX is designed.

options.title: Decline local execution
options.body: Keep CodexBar observability-only and direct automation users toward polling or the existing local serve interface instead of launching commands.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after argv repair
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in direct-exec design after the settings editor preserves argument boundaries and focused proof covers the repaired round trip.

likelyOwner.reason: As repository owner, steipete is the clearest available authority for accepting or rejecting this new persistent command-execution boundary.
